aggressive_definition: Palpable and anaplastic prostate tumors, contrasted with tumors incidentally discovered during surgery for benign prostatic hyperplasia or well-differentiated tumors
aggressive_definition_excerpt: In men > or = 57 years of age, 1,25-D was an important predictor of risk for palpable and anaplastic tumors but not for tumors incidentally discovered during surgery to treat the symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia or well differentiated tumors.
study_design: Matched nested case-control study using prediagnostic stored serum collected before prostate cancer diagnosis
reason: Prediagnostic vitamin D metabolites were evaluated for overall prostate cancer risk, and the abstract separately reports risk patterns for palpable and anaplastic tumors, an aggressive incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Risk of prostate cancer decreased with higher levels of 1,25-D especially in men with low levels of 25-D.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied row represents prostate cancer overall rather than the separately described palpable and anaplastic tumor endpoint.

additional_estimates.comparison: Serum 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D levels among men aged 57 years or older; specific contrast not reported
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: In men > or = 57 years of age, 1,25-D was an important predictor of risk for palpable and anaplastic tumors but not for tumors incidentally discovered during surgery to treat the symptoms of benign prostatic hyperplasia or well differentiated tumors.

validation_findings: Nested case-control/case-cohort analytic denominator must not be forced to full-cohort N
